learning_objective: 🎯 Learn that true sportsmanship and human compassion are far more valuable than simply winning a race or a gold medal!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The poem describes a 100-yard dash at the Special Olympics. Nine differently-abled athletes have trained for months, and now they stand at the starting line, waiting for the pistol to fire.
As soon as the race begins, the youngest athlete loses his balance, stumbles, and falls to the ground. His dreams and years of hard work are shattered, and he cries out in anguish.
In a fiercely competitive race, athletes usually keep running to win. But here, the other eight runners hear the boy's cry, stop in their tracks, and turn back to help him.
The eight athletes lift the fallen boy to his feet. They join hands and walk the remaining distance together. The competitive 'dash' turns into a beautiful 'walk' of unity.
Because they crossed the finish line together, holding hands, all nine athletes are awarded a gold medal. They all became winners, showing that empathy is the highest human achievement.

fun_activity.title: 🤝 The Empathy Race
fun_activity.instructions: Next time you play a game or a race with your friends, try waiting for the slowest person and crossing the finish line holding hands. Notice how it makes everyone feel like a winner!

exam_tips: 📌 Know the name of the poet: David Roth.
📌 Describe the contrast between what usually happens in a race (competition) and what happened in this poem (cooperation).
📌 Explain why the banner 'Special Olympics' was perfectly justified by the 'special' behavior of the athletes.
quick_recap: ⭐ The poem teaches us that helping others is a bigger victory than personal glory.
⭐ The fallen boy's cry of frustration turned into a smile because of his fellow athletes.
⭐ Empathy and sportsmanship are the ultimate gold medals of life.
